headline: Two Truths and a Lie Activity Powered by AI for ESL Classes
outcomes: Students practise evaluating claims and making arguments for their reasoning in English
Build critical thinking skills by analysing plausibility, language cues, and logical consistency
Develop listening comprehension as students process and compare three similar statements
Encourage natural discussion and justification using target vocabulary from the lesson topic
howItWorks: The AI generates three statements about the chosen topic — two factually true, one convincingly false
Students discuss which statement is the fabrication and vote on their device
Results are revealed alongside a full explanation of why the fabricated statement was incorrect
The reveal often generates spontaneous discussion, especially when the class is split on the answer
teacherUseCases: Content-area English lesson — students learn real facts while practising critical evaluation
Listening or reading comprehension extension where students apply judgment to propositions
Vocabulary review — the statements embed lesson vocabulary in plausible factual claims

faq.a: No. The AI is instructed to make the fabrication plausible and the true statements surprising, so students can't rely on 'this sounds too weird to be real.' The best rounds produce a genuine 50/50 class split.

faq.q: Can I use real facts or must I trust the AI?
faq.a: The AI generates factually grounded content, but for exam classes or factually sensitive subjects you can review and edit the statements before the round starts.

faq.q: How does this build English skills and not just general knowledge?
faq.a: The discussion phase is where the English learning happens. Students must articulate why they believe a statement is false, using hedging language, contrast, and logical connectors in real-time speech.

faq.q: Do students vote from their own phone?
faq.a: Yes — students vote on their phone or tablet through a browser. No app or download needed. They join via the teacher's shared link.

Science, history, geography, food culture, and business all work well — any domain where there are surprising true facts and plausible myths. The more the students care about the topic, the richer the discussion.

faq.q: Is Two Truths and a Fabrication free?
faq.a: Yes, Two Truths and a Fabrication is free. Students join via a shared browser link — no account setup or app download required.
